strings.d1.s0.name: Marmaris Castle
strings.d1.s0.tips: Suleiman the Magnificent's fortress with a small archaeology museum. It's cool in the morning, with marina views from the walls. Museum Pass accepted.
strings.d1.s1.name: Marmaris Bazaar
strings.d1.s1.tips: The old bazaar below the castle sells honey, leather and textiles. Haggling is normal.
strings.d1.s2.name: Icmeler Beach
strings.d1.s2.tips: A 15-minute dolmus (shared minibus) ride from Marmaris. The bay is shallow, calm and clean, sunbeds cost extra, and there is a free public beach section.
strings.d1.s3.name: Icmeler Bazaar Fish Restaurant
strings.d1.s3.tips: Fish and meze on the Icmeler seafront. Good for a late lunch after the beach.
strings.d1.s4.name: Marmaris Netsel Marina
strings.d1.s4.tips: Stroll the marina for yachts, cafes and sunset, with restaurants for dinner.
strings.d1.b0.name: Marmaris Fishermen's Harbour Restaurant
strings.d1.b0.tips: A fish restaurant in the centre.
strings.d1.b1.name: Marmaris Public Beach
strings.d1.b1.tips: A free beach on the central seafront and an alternative to Icmeler.
strings.d2.theme: Boat trip: Kizkumu, Selimiye and Orhaniye
strings.d2.s0.name: Kizkumu Beach
strings.d2.s0.tips: Take the 09:30 boat from Marmaris (about 1,000 TL, lunch and drinks included). It's a sandbar in the middle of the sea in Orhaniye Bay, where you walk 600 m through the water.
strings.d2.s1.name: Selimiye Bay
strings.d2.s1.tips: Lunch and swimming on the boat. The bay is calm, with a village jetty.
strings.d2.s2.name: Cleopatra Island
strings.d2.s2.tips: The last swim stop, with a small island and clear water. The return is at 18:00.
strings.d2.s3.name: Marmaris Kordon Fish Restaurant
strings.d2.s3.tips: Fish along the seafront strip. A good evening option after the boat trip.
strings.d2.b0.name: Marmaris Harbour Meyhane
strings.d2.b1.name: Rabbit Island
strings.d2.b1.tips: An alternative island stop on the tour route.
strings.d3.s0.name: Turunc Beach
strings.d3.s0.tips: 30 minutes from Marmaris by dolmus or water bus. A pine-scented bay with deep, clear water. Sunbeds cost extra.
strings.d3.s1.name: Turunc Seafront Restaurant
strings.d3.s1.tips: Grilled fish and meze on the seafront.
strings.d3.s2.name: Kumlubuk Beach
strings.d3.s2.tips: A quieter sandy bay behind Turunc. Swim at sunset.
strings.d3.s3.name: Amos Ancient City
strings.d3.s3.tips: A hill above Kumlubuk with a theatre and sunset views. Allow a 20-minute climb.
strings.d3.b0.name: Turunc Village Breakfast
strings.d3.b0.tips: Gozleme (stuffed flatbread) in a village house.
strings.d3.b1.name: Turunc Waterfall
strings.d3.b1.tips: A small waterfall behind the village, reached on foot.
strings.d4.s0.name: Selimiye Village
strings.d4.s0.tips: A fishing village on the Bozburun Peninsula with stone houses, a marina and a quiet bay. Stop for coffee.
strings.d4.s1.name: Selimiye Public Beach
strings.d4.s1.tips: The village beach, with calm water and free entry.
strings.d4.s2.name: Sardunya Restaurant Selimiye
strings.d4.s2.tips: Selimiye's seafront restaurant, serving seafood borek (filled pastry) and meze.
strings.d4.s3.name: Bozburun Marina
strings.d4.s3.tips: A village known for its wooden gulet boatyards. Walk the marina at sunset.
strings.d4.b0.name: Bozburun Fish Restaurant
strings.d4.b1.name: Sogut Village Beach
strings.d4.b1.tips: A quiet village beach beyond Bozburun.
strings.d5.s0.name: Gunnucek Nature Park
strings.d5.s0.tips: A forest of sweetgum trees next to Marmaris. Walk in the morning for the shade.
strings.d5.s1.name: Paradise Island Beach
strings.d5.s1.tips: Reach it by water bus from Marmaris or by car. There is a bay and a beach club, with boats to the Phosphorescent Cave.
strings.d5.s2.name: Paradise Island Restaurant
strings.d5.s2.tips: The island restaurant serves grills and salads.
strings.d5.s3.name: Marmaris Ataturk Statue Beach
strings.d5.s3.tips: An evening walk on the central seafront, with ice cream and sunset.
strings.d5.b0.name: Marmaris Bazaar Kofte Restaurant
strings.d5.b0.tips: Kofte with piyaz (bean salad) in the bazaar.
strings.d5.b1.name: Nimara Cave
strings.d5.b1.tips: A prehistoric cave on Paradise Island, reached on foot.
strings.d6.s0.name: Kaunos Ancient City
strings.d6.s0.tips: 1.5 hours from Marmaris. A Carian city reached by boat from Dalyan, with rock tombs across the river.
strings.d6.s1.name: Iztuzu Beach
strings.d6.s1.tips: A loggerhead turtle (caretta) nesting beach with 4.5 km of sand. Sunbeds cost extra, you can come by boat or dolmus, and shade is scarce.
strings.d6.s2.name: Dalyan Bazaar Fish Restaurant
strings.d6.s2.tips: Fish beside the Dalyan river, with a view of the rock tombs.
strings.d6.s3.name: Dalyan Rock Tombs
strings.d6.s3.tips: Lycian rock tombs seen from the riverbank. A good photo spot.
strings.d6.b0.name: Dalyan Mud Baths
strings.d6.b0.tips: The Sultaniye hot springs and mud, as an alternative to the beach.
strings.d6.b1.name: Dalyan Koyum Restaurant
strings.d7.theme: Marmaris morning and a gentle goodbye
strings.d7.s0.name: Marmaris Friday Market
strings.d7.s0.tips: On a Friday, expect a big market (honey, herbs, textiles). Otherwise, head to the Marmaris covered bazaar.
strings.d7.s1.name: Marmaris Honey House
strings.d7.s1.tips: Taste and buy Marmaris pine honey, with breakfast.
strings.d7.s2.name: Marmaris Seafront Promenade
strings.d7.s2.tips: One last walk from the castle to the marina.
strings.d7.s3.name: Marmaris Kordon Tea Garden
strings.d7.s3.tips: Tea and toast by the sea for a farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Marmaris Bazaar Breakfast Place
strings.d7.b1.name: Marmaris Marina Bazaar
strings.note0: From central Marmaris, dolmus and water buses run to Icmeler, Turunc and Paradise Island. For Selimiye-Bozburun and Dalyan, a car is the most practical option.
strings.note1: Buy boat tours from the seafront stalls the day before (about 1,000 TL, lunch included). Bring shallow-water shoes for Kizkumu.
strings.note2: Summer heat reaches 38°C: swim between 12:00 and 16:00 and visit the ancient cities in the morning.
strings.note3: Marmaris pine honey and seafood borek are local specialities. Haggling in the bazaar is normal.
strings.note4: Public beaches in the centre, Icmeler and Selimiye are free. Beach club sunbeds cost 300-1,000 TL.
strings.note5: Dalaman Airport is 1.5 hours away. The Havas airport bus leaves from the bus station.
